b2-18-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Ana Told Me
b2-18-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what a colleague of yours said after the meeting. She admitted that she had made a mistake and added that she would call again.
b2-18-01.prompt: Tell Meg what your colleague said after the meeting.
b2-18-01.target: Mi compañera admitió que se había equivocado y añadió que llamaría otra vez.
b2-18-01.english: My colleague admitted that she had made a mistake and added that she would call again.
b2-18-01.canDo: I can choose a reporting verb that says how something was said (afirmar, explicar, añadir, admitir, negar, advertir, recordar, reprochar, sugerir).

b2-18-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Saw the Message
b2-18-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what two of your classmates said about a message. One denied having seen it, and the other answered back that he had read it.
b2-18-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what your two classmates said.
b2-18-02.target: Un compañero negó haber visto el mensaje, pero otra compañera replicó que lo había leído.
b2-18-02.english: One classmate denied having seen the message, but another answered back that he had read it.
b2-18-02.canDo: I can report a denial with negar que + subjunctive or negar + haber + participle, and an admission with admitir que + indicative.

b2-18-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Storm
b2-18-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you closed all the windows. A colleague warned you that there would be a storm and reminded you to close them.
b2-18-03.prompt: Tell Meg what your colleague said.
cues: Report her warning about the weather
Report what she reminded you to do
b2-18-03.target: Mi compañera me advirtió que habría una tormenta y me recordó que cerrara las ventanas.
b2-18-03.english: My colleague warned me that there would be a storm and reminded me to close the windows.
b2-18-03.canDo: I can report a warning or a reminder of a fact with advertir or recordar + que + indicative.

b2-18-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Ana Is Upset
b2-18-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why a classmate of yours is upset with you. She reproached you for not having called her, and she blamed you for the delay.
b2-18-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what your classmate said.
cues: Report her reproach about the call
Say what she blamed you for
b2-18-04.target: Mi compañera me reprochó que no la hubiera llamado y me culpó del retraso.
b2-18-04.english: My classmate reproached me for not having called her and blamed me for the delay.
b2-18-04.canDo: I can report a reproach with reprochar or echar en cara + que + subjunctive.

b2-18-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Is the Shop Closed?
b2-18-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if the shop has closed. A neighbour says it closed last month, but nobody has confirmed it.
b2-18-05.prompt: Tell Meg what you heard, without saying it is certain.
cues: Say who told you that the shop closed
Say that it is not confirmed
b2-18-05.target: Según un vecino, la tienda cerró el mes pasado, pero al parecer nadie lo ha confirmado.
b2-18-05.english: According to a neighbour, the shop closed last month, but apparently nobody has confirmed it.
b2-18-05.canDo: I can report a claim without saying it is true, with según, al parecer, supuestamente and presunto.

b2-18-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Ana’s Book
b2-18-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what a classmate of yours said about a novel she read. She said it was very hard, admitted that she had taken a month to read it, and reminded you to read it slowly.
b2-18-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what your classmate said about the novel.
cues: Report what she stated about the novel
Report what she reminded you to do
b2-18-consolidation.target: Mi compañera afirmó que la novela era muy difícil y admitió que había tardado un mes en leerla. Me recordó que la leyera con calma.
b2-18-consolidation.english: My classmate stated that the novel was very hard and admitted that she had taken a month to read it. She reminded me to read it calmly.
b2-18-consolidation.canDo: I can choose the reporting verb and the mood for statements, denials, warnings and reproaches.
